text:
morgan (pm): Quick thread: customers keep asking for a clear tenant-slicing roadmap that balances cost vs isolation. Need a concise launch checklist + migration path by next Tue.

diego (eng-plat): My recommended approach: define a "slicing ladder" (shared -> burst-reserve -> reserved-pool -> private). Each rung must have: acceptance metrics, billing shape, and rollback action.

harper (infra): Implementation options: (A) soft tokens layered on shared pools, (B) carved node pools per tenant. Tokens are faster to ship, carved pools give cleaner SLAs. Both need warm-slot planning.

noah (sre): Ops asks: for each rung we need a chaos scenario, abort criteria, and an automated rollback (eg revoke reservation and fallback to shared). Example abort: p99 increase > 2x baseline or user error spike >0.5%.

leila (sales): Pilot asks: two prospects will pay for reserved-pool if we guarantee monthly cost cap + simple overage rules. Sales wants a price multiplier table (1x, 2.5x, 4x) -> expected p95/p99 improvements to show ROI.

anya (research): Model note: some quantization levels have worse cold-start behavior on our fastest kernels. We'll publish a compact compat appendix that maps model_variant -> recommended lane.

diego (eng-plat): API sketch for policy + migration command:
```
redwood policy set --tenant acme --tier burst-reserve --regions us-west-2,eu-west-1 --capacity 256GB --fallback nearest
redwood migrate --from shared --to reserved-pool --tenant acme --dry-run
```
Console should show estimated monthly delta and warm-slot suggestion.

morgan (pm): Proposed acceptance gates per rung (MVP):
- burst-reserve: policy API + telemetry + perf harness p95 < 160ms; canary 48h; billing hooks enforce soft quota within 60s.
- reserved-pool: pool allocator + warm-slot validated; canary tenant on reserved pool 72h; billing enforcement + monthly invoice preview.
- private: private control plane + KMS + install runbook; compliance checklist pass.

harper (infra): Risk: if we under-size warm slots, dedicated pools cause token latency spikes during bursts. Will run cost sims to recommend warm-slot sizes per tenant profile.

noah (sre): Telemetry event request: emit "slice.fallback" with fields tenant, origin_lane, fallback_model, latency_ms, region. This will let quality and billing teams correlate. Also create automated alert when cross-region spill rate > 3% for a tenant.

billing-bot: Note: billing hooks required for reserved-pool: 60s enforcement window + invoice preview endpoint. Finance needs to define overage tiers.

leila (sales): I'll draft the price-vs-latency one-pager and include a migration credit option for first-month commit. Coordinate with finance for overage language.

anya (research): I'll provide a 1-page compatibility matrix and a short note on quality delta for fallback variants. Add that as a required acceptance item.

diego (eng-plat): Dependencies: research compatibility, runtime warm-start API, infra pool allocator and egress caps, billing quota APIs, console estimator. Assigning owners in the decision doc helps.

morgan (pm): I'll write the decision doc with the ladder, gates, and owners. Draft due Mon noon so Sales has something for pilot talks. Anything else?

deploy-bot: canary deploy for policy-service started on staging at 1901234688 :rocket:

harper (infra): I'll run cost sims and post numbers under /shared/cost-sims/1901234567 within 48h.

noah (sre): I'll draft the chaos matrix and schedule a red-team eviction against staging reserved-pool. Will include explicit rollback steps.

morgan (pm): Great. I'll ping legal/finance for billing wording and include the telemetry event in the spec. PR incoming.
